title: Library visit list
intro: Records that can only be settled by a visit (or by staff retrieval on request), collected from the dossiers. Read-only planning list: no visit, call, e-mail or records request has been made. Phoning ahead or filing a records request is an outside contact and needs Nathan's go-ahead first. Holdings and access terms are NEEDS_VERIFICATION unless a dossier already cites them. Every item stays open in its dossier until the record itself is seen.

findings: **Record gap (finding, 2026-10-04): no surviving San Francisco civil death register covers 1 May 1873 – 31 Mar 1882 (SFgenealogy listing, quoted); the April 1882+ volume is coroner cases only.** SFgenealogy's entry for the 'Record of Deaths (aka Mortuary Record of the City and County of San Francisco and Register of Deaths of the City and County of San Francisco), 1865-1904' (https://sfgenealogy.org/doku.php?id=san_francisco_county:offline (fetched 2026-10-04 10:35 PT; copy in visitlist-work/src/)) lists '08 Nov 1865 - 30 Sep 1869, Volume 1 (…) 01 Oct 1869 - 30 Apr 1873, Volume 2 (…) 01 Apr 1882 - 30 Jun 1889, Volume 3 (Coroner Cases Only) and Index' ('(…)' stands for the index and holder notes). Newhall died on 13 Mar 1882, inside the gap, so no civil death record of his death is known to survive, and the cause and age as certified cannot come from that source (C13, C1). Library visit list item V6 is removed (kept visible there). Leads: V6a, the Laurel Hill Cemetery (San Francisco) Registers, held by the Society of California Pioneers (they may also bear on the open date of his removal to Cypress Lawn, C14); V6b, original funeral records, pre-1920, at the SFPL History Center. Whether either records a cause of death is NEEDS_VERIFICATION.

items.where: Archdiocese of Los Angeles Archival Center, Mission Hills (originals); Huntington Library (microfilm). Copies of the San Fernando and Plaza Church registers are also at the Santa Barbara Mission Archive-Library (Perkins triage). The Archival Center admits accredited researchers; access terms NEEDS_VERIFICATION.

items.purpose: Confirm the ECPP index entry against the register image: Antonio del Valle buried at Mission San Fernando on 3 June 1841 (so he died on or before that date). The register may also give a death date, which the index leaves blank.

items.look_at: Santa Barbara Presidio baptismal register: baptism 00917, 4 Jul 1831 (ECPP id 976).
items.purpose: Confirm the ECPP index entry against the register image.
items.known: Contradicted 2026-10-04 on both counts, as far as the ECPP index shows [ECPP record pages as read by the user in a browser session, 2026-10-04 ~02:55 PT; the burial and the Magdalena baptism checked by the user against screenshots; ECPP is an index/transcription, register images not seen]. What the baptism says: 'Maria Magdalena Antonia', baptized 4 Jul 1831 at the Santa Barbara Presidio, born the day before ('el dia anterior como a las nueve de la noche'); father 'Antonio' 'Valles' (recorded as a widower); mother María Policarpa López. That 'Antonio Valles' is Antonio del Valle is an inference (NEEDS_VERIFICATION). Whether she was Ygnacio's full or half sister is not shown in these records.

items.where: LA County Board of Supervisors, Executive Office, Records Management Section (Hahn Hall of Administration). Its web page says the minute books go back to 1852, records from 1873 are digitized, and pre-1985 records are retrieved on request (213-974-1424); phone first (an outside contact: needs Nathan's go-ahead). Seaver Center (NHM) GC 1164 holds only Board book no. 1 (1852–55).
items.look_at: Board minute book covering May 1869 (La Rue's appointment as JP of Soledad Township), and the entry that created Soledad Township (date unknown; search 1866–69). Minute-book volume numbers are not known (NEEDS_VERIFICATION).
items.purpose: P26: confirm the appointment entry; whether La Rue was the first Soledad JP depends on whether the township's creation is minuted. Perkins C13: the start of the Soledad township justice (Board minutes 1869–75).
items.known: LA Daily News, 12 May 1869 (Board proceedings, CDNC OCR via the user's browser search): La Rue appointed JP for Soledad Township on petition. No earlier Soledad JP found.

items.where: San Francisco Public Library, San Francisco History Center. Which years it holds, and in what form, is NEEDS_VERIFICATION (check the catalog or phone first; phoning is an outside contact).
items.look_at: San Francisco city directories for 1852 (Parker), 1856 (Colville), 1858–59 (Langley) and 1864–82 (Langley): the alphabetical entries for Newhall and the firm (also Gregory, Claghorn, Eldridge, Palache, Van Pelt). None of these years is in full view on HathiTrust (catalog checked 2026-10-04).
items.purpose: C4: the start dates of stage 2 (Newhall, Gregory & Co., first use, attested by Aug 1854), stage 3 (Newhall, Gregory & Claghorn, in the 1854 directory, ended 1 Jan 1855) and stage 6 (Newhall, Gregory & Co. again, after Gregory rejoined between 1 Jan 1858 and 4 Jan 1860); the 1852 and 1858–59 directories are the ones that matter. The change to H. M. Newhall & Co. is settled: 4 Jan 1860 (dissolution notice, Daily Alta California, 5 Jan 1860). C5: his S.F. & S.J. Railroad office, 1864–70. C15: Newhall's Sons & Co. and H. M. Newhall & Co., 1881–82.
items.known: Read 2026-10-04 on HathiTrust: Kimball 1850 ('Hall & Martin, auctioneers, Jackson'; no Newhall), LeCount & Strong 1854 ('Newhall, Gregory & Claghorn'), Langley 1860, 1861, 1862 and 1863/64 ('NEWHALL H. M. & CO.'; J. Oscar Eldridge named from 1862). Newhall dossier section 5.1, R1–R7. The firm's own notices in the Daily Alta (CDNC): 'Newhall & Hall's building' (17 Apr 1852); Newhall, Gregory & Claghorn expired 1 Jan 1855, followed by Newhall & Gregory (notice of 11 Mar 1855); Newhall, Gregory & Co. dissolved 4 Jan 1860, followed by H. M. Newhall & Co. (notice of 5 Jan 1860). Newhall dossier section 5.1, R18–R22. Also: San Joaquin Republican, 11 Aug 1854 ('recently occupied by Messrs. Newhall, Gregory & Co.'); Daily Alta, 7 Jan 1858 (Newhall & Gregory dissolved 1 Jan 1858; Newhall & Co., with E. W. Eddy, from that day). Newhall dossier section 5.1, R24–R25. The reading status of each record (confirmed at full zoom, image reading only, scan text only) is given there (Method).

items.where: San Francisco death register or coroner's register, March 1882. The Newhall dossier names the SF Public Library, San Francisco History Center; whether the 1882 registers survived the 1906 fire, and who holds them, is NEEDS_VERIFICATION.
items.look_at: The entry for Henry Mayo Newhall, died Monday 13 Mar 1882 at 1299 Van Ness Avenue (a coroner's entry exists only if the coroner took the case: NEEDS_VERIFICATION).
items.purpose: It may give the cause of death as certified, which no newspaper can (Nathan, 2026-10-04). That bears on C13, which stays a conflict: the papers name erysipelas (Sacramento Daily Union, San Jose Mercury-News, SF Chronicle) or blood-poisoning from the fall's injuries with his weakened system (Daily Alta), and C13 is not decided by counting them. Secondary: the age as recorded (C1, birth May 13 or May 23, 1825).
items.known: Death 13 Mar 1882, about 7 a.m., at his home; funeral 15 Mar, 11 a.m., from 1299 Van Ness Avenue; buried at Laurel Hill (1882 papers on CDNC, Newhall dossier section 5.1, R9–R17).
